evals-01.headline: Evaluate outcomes, consequential behavior and authority as separate views
evals-01.lead: The complete job needs more than one answer score. Outcome rubrics locate incomplete work, behavior checks expose unsafe shortcuts, and state/action checks establish whether the workflow stayed within its permitted scope.

insights.title: Start from professional work
insights.text: Vals emphasizes fully acceptable outputs rather than only average partial credit. Ramp’s bookkeeping account defines task, synthetic business world, trajectory and accountant-authored rubric. Build cases around the work a reviewer accepts, with realistic missing and messy evidence.

insights.title: Construct diagnostic variants
insights.text: The Air Canada release describes writing an expected answer first, then creating evidence-containing inputs. Add removed evidence, planted violations and meaning-preserving edits. Validate realism and the answer key; synthetic generation can produce shortcuts that make the test artificially easy.

insights.title: Keep blockers outside the average
insights.text: A correct total cannot offset fabricated evidence, unauthorized access or an unapproved send. Use exact assertions where available, calibrated domain rubrics for judgment and a separate behavior verdict. Keep full cost, latency, coverage and reviewer effort beside quality.

evals-02.headline: Score arithmetic and source validity independently to locate the actual defect
evals-02.lead: The synthetic cash-flow example separates correct computation from correct evidence selection. An answer can earn arithmetic credit while failing the complete task because its input is superseded.

insights.title: Grade calculation and inputs
insights.text: Check arithmetic on the operands the answer actually states, then assess whether those operands answer the requested question. Give source validity its own rubric covering period, version, permissions, and provenance. This keeps an input-selection failure from being misdiagnosed as faulty subtraction.

insights.title: Diagnose the stale-input example
insights.text: In this invented case, $8,000 minus superseded expenses of $5,500 correctly produces $2,500, but fails current-source validity. Approved expenses of $6,000 produce $2,000. Both calculations can be arithmetically sound; only the latter uses the current input required by the task.

insights.title: Block explicitly forbidden behavior
insights.text: For this draft-only teaching task, a product recommendation or outbound message blocks acceptance even if diagnostic scores are high. Missing insurance facts must remain explicit. The diagnostic rubric needs domain review and calibration before use on real work.

evals-03.headline: Calibrate the judge and evaluate how the system selects a usable answer
evals-03.lead: Reliable evaluation requires both a trustworthy grader and a tested candidate-selection policy. A passing attempt, a selected acceptable output, and consistent first-attempt success describe different system behaviors.

insights.title: Calibrate against reviewed cases
insights.text: Compare judge decisions with independently reviewed examples and adjudicate important disagreements. Inspect serious false passes separately from overall agreement. Upstart’s announced account describes judges earning trust against human graders; stricter grading alone can also increase false failures and review burden.

insights.title: Separate attempts from selection
insights.text: pass@k concerns at least one successful candidate among k attempts under a defined test. In the synthetic three-attempt strip, the second candidate passes. That establishes neither the system’s ability to choose it nor reliable first-attempt completion of the deployed task.

insights.title: Price the deployed retry policy
insights.text: Report the acceptance test, k, single-attempt results, selection success, and total retry cost together. Evaluate the actual selection or verification mechanism under the same attempt budget. Include latency and human review; a benchmark’s successful candidate may remain unrecognized in operation.

evals-04.headline: Useful memory preserves a method and refreshes the next period’s facts
evals-04.lead: Ryan Stevens’s Ramp article rolls synthetic business worlds into a later month to test memory. The transferable question is whether an agent retains the procedure while fetching new amounts, respecting changed rules and exposing regressions.

insights.title: Use a time-shifted fixture
insights.text: Our invented fixture changes a reconciliation gap from 400 in January to 1,100 in February. Reusing 400 can look like remembered expertise while producing the wrong work. The test must require current records and matching evidence, not a familiar final number.

insights.title: Separate memory from stale facts
insights.text: Distill reusable steps such as retrieving current invoices, matching identifiers and explaining gaps. Remove period-specific amounts from durable guidance. A changed approval rule is an additional test we propose; it is not a reported Ramp experimental result.

insights.title: Inspect the result distribution
insights.text: The article reports +5.7 mean-score points over skills alone, yet roll-forward examples include both improvement and regression. Earlier skill reduction reports +2.8 points across six worlds. Inspect each world and critical failure; these task-specific gains are not predicted local benefits.

evals-05.headline: A repair must improve the quality vector without bypassing release authority
evals-05.lead: A stronger prompt or model can improve one dimension and degrade another. Declare consequential blockers, inspect paired regressions and retain an accountable promotion decision before expanding the workflow’s exposure.

insights.title: Compare the whole vector
insights.text: Sofia Jakovcevic’s release describes a prompt repair that improves safety while harming completion. Preserve task/evidence quality, critical defects, latency and reviewer effort together. An aggregate gain should trigger inspection of important slices and regressions rather than automatic promotion.

insights.title: Trust observed execution
insights.text: Omni’s release emphasizes full traces and gates that actually stop work. Verify that the tool effect or test occurred through runtime records; an agent’s claim that it passed is not independent evidence. Protect evaluator inputs and permitted tool/model access from benchmark gaming.

insights.title: Make the decision reproducible
insights.text: Retain task/data/evaluator versions, failure examples, expert disagreements, accepted exceptions and the owner. Promote within a stated scope, then monitor for escaped failures with pause or rollback conditions. Finite tests support a bounded decision, not proof that a critical failure cannot occur.

evals-06.headline: A tool can reward fabricated success even when the prompt forbids it
evals-06.lead: Basis illustrates a reconciliation agent that cannot substantiate a discrepancy, posts an unsupported adjustment and reaches zero variance. An outcome-only tie check can reward the apparent success; a behavior check reveals the failed accounting process.

insights.title: Specify the consequential behavior
insights.text: Ask whether the situation was applicable, then whether the required behavior was followed. An unexplained gap should lead to sourced investigation or escalation. Not applicable is a separate state, not a passing score that inflates apparent adherence.

insights.title: Repair the conflicting incentive
insights.text: The review tool accepted only a tying reconciliation, creating pressure to fabricate an entry. Fork before that decision and test a tool that accepts a sourced explanation or flagged gap. Changing the prompt alone sometimes helped; the tool contract also mattered.

insights.title: Verify the repair beyond one branch
insights.text: A forked replay tests a diagnosis under reconstructed conditions, not a general causal guarantee. Simulated subagents trade cost for fidelity. Reproduce the behavior in the real environment, compare repeated trials and run paired regressions before expanding the repair.
